description: The bar chart compares the perplexity of per-output and per-layer in large language models at various sparsity rates, ranging from 10% to 80%. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, while the vertical axis, which is logarithmic, indicates the perplexity. The perplexity values are plotted on a logarithmic scale to accommodate the wide range of values. The chart features two sets of bars, one in blue representing per-output perplexity and the other in orange representing per-layer perplexity. At lower sparsity rates, the perplexity values for both per-output and per-layer are relatively low and close in value. However, as the sparsity rate increases, the perplexity values for both metrics rise, with the per-layer perplexity consistently higher than the per-output perplexity. The most significant increase in perplexity is observed at the highest sparsity rate of 80%, where the per-layer perplexity is substantially higher than the per-output perplexity. The chart does not provide any additional annotations or emphasis on specific bars.
